clue.text: Note deposit required by one finally providing credit

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to deposit something is to put it down

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word one

explanation.surface: A bank wants a deposit before it will grant someone credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E, the last letter of 'one'; 'required by' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is good standing or reputation, and credit in the sense of honour or esteem is a synonym.

clue.text: Philosopher heard making little noise

indicators.note: heard means the name is spoken, and its sound gives the letters entered

parts.note: Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker is said to make hardly any sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft crackling sound, such as dry leaves make, so it is a slight noise.

clue.text: Frugal poet stopping penny payment

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the poet's name fills the space inside the other pieces

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property
Ovid was a Roman poet

explanation.surface: A thrifty poet halts a penny payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' looks like a verb about the poet, but it puts the poet's name between the penny and the payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Provident means saving carefully for the future, which is close in sense to thrifty or frugal.

clue.text: Impose restrictions on use of moor

definitions.meaning: to bind money or assets so they cannot be freely used
to fasten a boat to a post or quay

explanation.surface: Ban the use of open moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moor' looks like open moorland, but it is the verb for securing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Money tied up in a deal is restricted; a boat tied up at a quay is moored.

clue.text: Allies set out to capture a British or Spanish queen

indicators.note: to capture means to hold inside, so the other letters go into the middle of the rearranged word
set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of Allies are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Allied forces set out to seize a queen of Britain or Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' turns the letters of 'Allies' into ISELLA. 'British or' looks like part of the definition, but 'British' supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella of Castile was the Spanish queen who sponsored Columbus, so the name is an example of the type.

clue.text: She's eye-pleasing but out

indicators.note: out means out of place, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: She is lovely to look at but is unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EYE-PLEASING BUT, and also describes the fairytale heroine, who is out cold and lovely to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairytale princess is a female figure, so the pronoun she can stand for her here.

clue.text: Game interrupted by female reporter in 1942

indicators.note: interrupted by means the game's name is broken open by the next piece

parts.note: bridge is a card game
Eve, the first woman in Genesis, often stands for a female

explanation.surface: A card game is broken off by a woman journalist in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: Beveridge's report of 1942 is the joke: 'reporter' means the author of that report, not a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: William Beveridge wrote the 1942 Beveridge Report, the plan behind Britain's welfare state, so he was a reporter then.

clue.text: Letters from Sackville-West somewhere in Sussex

indicators.note: letters from asks for a run of consecutive letters taken from the name that follows

explanation.surface: Vita Sackville-West sent letters from somewhere in Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: Vita Sackville-West was an English writer who lived in Kent and Sussex. LEWES is the county town of East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex, so it is one particular place in that county.

clue.text: Rock it and see crack

indicators.note: crack means to break, so the letters of the three words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Have a look at the rock and see the crack.
explanation.definitionFit: Andesite is a fine-grained volcanic rock named after the Andes, so it is one particular kind of rock.

clue.text: Governor-General connected tunnels before battle

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: a warren is a network of linked burrows
Hastings, 1066, is the famous battle in which William the Conqueror won England

explanation.surface: An official network of tunnels ahead of a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of British India, from 1773.

clue.text: Original article in outlet for pottery

indicators.note: in means the words before it are placed inside the word for outlet

parts.note: a store is a retail outlet, a shop
something original is new, never seen before
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A new item is placed in a shop that sells pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' looks like it describes the article, but it supplies its own word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a kind of dense fired pottery, so the answer is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Day after Victor and Oscar initially took the pledge

indicators.note: after means the day's abbreviation follows the two letters
initially asks for the opening letter of each of the two names Victor and Oscar

parts.note: Wed is the short form of Wednesday, a day of the week

explanation.surface: A day after Victor and Oscar first signed up to abstain from drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took the pledge' suggests giving up alcohol, but here it simply means made a solemn promise.
explanation.definitionFit: To have vowed is to have made a solemn promise, which is what taking a pledge means.

clue.text: Flower arrangement regularly seen in Algeria

indicators.note: regularly seen in picks the second, fourth and sixth letters of Algeria

explanation.surface: Floral displays are commonly seen across Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers, literally flowers arranged into a necklace.

clue.text: A sharp spear being thrown changes one's expression

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone hurls a sharp spear and their face changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a change of facial look, but here it means rewording what one has said.
explanation.definitionFit: To paraphrase is to restate something in other words, which changes how it is expressed.

clue.text: Fisher's first from boat in Biblical city

indicators.note: in means the picked letter goes inside the bird's name

parts.note: a heron is a wading bird that fishes, so it is a fisher

indicators.note: first from asks for the opening letter of the word boat

explanation.surface: An angler's first catch from the boat in a Bible city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fisher' looks like an angler but is a bird that fishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebron is an ancient city in the West Bank that features often in the Bible, as Abraham's burial place.

clue.text: After a few drinks see about a song

indicators.note: after says the following piece comes after the drinks

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the bishop's seat goes around the letter

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see, in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: After a few drinks, take a look at a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb but is the diocese of ELY, which goes around A to make ELAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a simple song with a refrain, so it is one particular kind of song.

clue.text: Surely bound to work

indicators.note: work as a verb means to knead or shape, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: It is certain to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to work' reads as 'certain to succeed', but 'work' rearranges the letters of BOUND TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of certainty: saying something will happen without doubt means it will surely happen.

clue.text: Capital drug trial

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
a case is a legal action tried in court

explanation.surface: A big drug trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city or money, but means capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are the large ones; printers kept them in the upper case of type.

clue.text: Gauge showing one mile covered by car

indicators.note: covered by means the two pieces sit inside the word for a car

parts.note: an estate is an estate car, the British name for a station wagon
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Measure how a car covers a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' puts I and M inside ESTATE after ESTI; 'showing' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge approximately, as to gauge also means to make a rough measurement.

clue.text: University graduate tests first fruit

indicators.note: first says the word for tests is placed before the other two pieces

parts.note: SATs are standard school tests
an MA, a Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A university graduate takes tests before eating fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' sends SATS to the front, though it is printed last.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, like a mandarin, so it is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Audible signals at side of bed disturbed sleep

indicators.note: side of asks for an edge letter of the word bed, here its first
disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of sleep are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beeps from the bedside alarm broke someone's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side of' gives B; 'disturbed' turns SLEEP into LEEPS; 'at' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is a short high electronic tone, so the plural form names audible signals of that kind.

clue.text: Least successful position for weaver

definitions.meaning: the lowest place, as at the foot of a league table
Nick ..., the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: The worst place for a weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: Last place in a ranking is the lowest; and the Shakespeare weaver bears this name.

clue.text: Advantageous position where car is reversed?

definitions.text: Advantageous position where car is reversed?

parts.words: Advantageous position where car is reversed?
parts.note: a favoured spot on a running course, read as a picture: the word car turned back sits within the word for a course

explanation.surface: A good place on a circuit where a car is driven backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: RAC (car backwards) sits inside the word TRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the inside lane on a race course gives the shorter route, hence any position of advantage.

clue.text: Doesn't take off underwear

definitions.meaning: a corset stiffened with bones, worn as underclothing

explanation.surface: Someone never takes off their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that remains stays; stays are also an old corset.

clue.text: Whip revealed by characters in Heart of Darkness

indicators.note: characters in heart of asks for the two middle letters of the word Darkness

parts.note: something revealed is out, in the open

explanation.surface: A whip shows up in Conrad's novel Heart of Darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: The book title is a trap: 'Heart of' picks KN from the middle of DARKNESS; 'by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout is a type of whip once used in Russia to flog criminals.

clue.text: Crow not the last companion of Pooh

indicators.note: not the last means the closing letter is dropped from the bird's name

parts.note: a rook is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A crow, not the last of Pooh's friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove K, the last letter of ROOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Roo, the young kangaroo, is one of Winnie-the-Pooh's friends in A. A. Milne's stories.

clue.text: A cover said to be of use

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, and the spoken form is what goes in the grid

parts.note: a veil is a cover over the face

explanation.surface: A covering is claimed to be useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A veil' said aloud sounds like the answer; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to help or benefit, which is what being of use means.

clue.text: Wait when Ingham has left city without furniture?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the shortened city goes around the furniture
has left means those letters are gone from the city's name

parts.note: Nottingham is an English city in the East Midlands
sofas are items of furniture

explanation.surface: Wait: if Ingham moves out, is the city left with no furniture?
explanation.walkthrough: Ingham looks like a person (Bernard Ingham, Thatcher's press secretary) but is the end of NOTTINGHAM; NOTT goes outside SOFAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying wait to stop someone rushing ahead is the same as the idiom telling them to slow down.

clue.text: Writer, possibly, is in centre of Fleet Street

indicators.note: centre of asks for the middle letter of the word Fleet
in means the two words before it go inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: say, as in for example, introduces a possibility

explanation.surface: A writer may well be found in the heart of Fleet Street, London's old newspaper district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes E from FLEET; 'in' puts SAY and IS inside ST. Fleet Street is the London street once home to the national newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist writes essays, so is one particular kind of writer.

clue.text: Some pupils play in real time

definitions.meaning: a school ability set, a group of pupils taught together
to broadcast audio or video live over the internet as it happens

explanation.surface: Some pupils perform live.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a stream is an ability group; online, to stream is to play media live as it arrives.
